*Update 10.11.2025*

* We spent €594k (Q1–Q3 actuals + Q4 projection) on new channel supply acquisition.
* We ran 31 experiments across 4 new channels: _Moloco, TradeDesk, Line,_ and _DV360_ during Q1-Q3 2025
* 35% (11 experiments) showed incrementality, confirmed via both platform-based experiments (CLS) and in-house experiments
* 14 additional experiments are planned for Q4 2025

h3. *Channel Highlights*

h4. *Moloco*

* Most promising channel, particularly in African markets
* Showed incrementality in 4 markets, with 11 experiments demonstrating uplift
* MMM allocated proper budgets only for GH and ZA, as unit economics in other markets were less favorable
* Decision: Continue testing in GH and ZA to improve efficiency, and expand tests to other markets where incrementality is difficult to detect through existing channels (Google, Meta, and TikTok)

h4. *TradeDesk*

* Tested in NG, GH, and ZA
* Limited experimental evidence; results were likely influenced by unstable spending patterns, with budgets unintentionally dropping to zero early in some months
* Decision: Pause further testing until channel stability and consistent budget delivery are ensured.

h4. *Line*

* Limited scale across markets; primarily suitable for TH, with potential extension to TW.
* No incrementality observed and limited scalability due to market constraints, and a lack of platform support from their representative.
* Decision: Stop testing and focus resources on higher-leverage channels and markets.

h4. *DV360*

* Tested in FR, TH, and UK
* Limited incrementality observed across tested markets
* Unlike TradeDesk, no major spending issues were observed.
* Decision: Continue testing to build stronger incrementality evidence in TH, as positive incrementality signals were observed in 2024 for this channel

Hi [~accountid:712020:714baa0e-ddd0-4776-8064-c5a5d3ae37aa], taking each question in turn, here are my replies: 

# *How flexible are the current termination provisions?*

Across both MSAs (2F: 2023; 3F+4F: 2025):

* Termination for breach/insolvency: Either party can terminate if the other breaches and doesn’t fix it within 28 days; standard insolvency triggers also apply.
* There is no “termination for convenience.” There’s no unilateral early-exit right just because we want to stop services. 
* Service suspension for non-payment: Kitt can suspend services on 14 days’ written notice if fees aren’t paid. (Worth softening this on renegotiation.)
* Underlet part after the Break Date (20 Jul 2026): We can require Kitt to reduce/discontinue services to that part and the fees reduce pro-rata. However, we know we are not going to be exercising the break right. 

*Where they differ:*

* If the underlying lease(s) end early
• 2F: the MSA automatically terminates when the lease ends.  
• 3F+4F: the MSA only terminates when both leases have ended. If one floor continues, the MSA stays alive and the fees drop to the continuing floor but not below £18,000 + VAT/month (a floor). 
* Assign/underlet the whole after the Break Date (20 Jul 2026): We may terminate on 3 months’ notice, but only after completing the assignment/underlease and after paying Kitt’s early-termination costs (they notify us of the amount). 
* Term alignment: 2F is tied to the lease “Contractual Term.” 3F+4F runs from “Operational Date” to “Term End Date,” but again the special rule above means we don’t get an automatic end unless both of those leases terminate.

# *Risks/implications if we re-open or amend now*

The above contract risks already exist today - I don’t think re-opening a conversation with Kitt creates any additional risk - but this depends on how we approach the conversation - if we frame it purely as a price squeeze it could create a relationship friction. They may try to extend beyond July 2028 or add auto-renew or ask for an uplift elsewhere. 

# *Recommended language to use*

We will not exercise the 2026 break and will remain at Old Street through July 2028. Given that certainty and the operational scale across three floors, we want to lock a lean, predictable run-rate while leaving the existing contract structure unchanged.

We spent *€3.04M* on new channel demand acquisition (Q1-Q3 actuals + Q4 projections). 

During the first three quarters of 2025, 31 new channel experiments were measured to evaluate incremental impact.

Discussed the requirements with [~accountid:712020:6a8c08e1-ab41-4fd9-afb9-e47c10d0b16b]. The idea is to be able to calculate the total time spent waiting on locks for the project (e.g. an Epic or group of tasks). The project might have multiple builder pipelines. Builder pipelines might have different PR names. Providing a fully automated solution might be quite expensive (in terms of effort). We agreed that the following functionality would be enough:

# Provide an internal endpoint to retrieve pipelines (ID’s) based on the PR name (full name or partial)
# Provide an internal endpoint to retrieve information about pipeline steps (e.g. step execution time) by pipeline ID

Having those endpoints would make it possible to:

# Find all release pipelines for a specific project
# Calculate the time spent acquiring locks (check execution time of the acquire lock step) based on the data from the get pipeline info

Acceptance criteria:

* Create an internal endpoint to retrieve pipelines (ID’s) based on the PR name (full name or partial)
* Create an internal endpoint to retrieve data about pipeline steps (step name and step execution time must be included) by the pipeline ID



Another option is to add missing data to the data lake. In this case, it must be possible to search pipelines by PR name (exact or partial match). And with pipeline ID’s, it must be possible to calculate step duration times. We already have some data in the data lake (e.g. pipelines and pipeline steps). But seems that we don’t have data about the PR name.

Hello,

The customer used an APM (Alternative Payment Method) to place the order and this type of payment methods does not have a preauthorisation option that is later reversed. They only support a direct charge on the card. So if the user makes an order but then cancels it, in this case we refund their money unlike preauthorisation where we just release the reserved amount. 
So in this case, the user placed an order and we charged them higher, but at the end of the ride, the order price decreased or the order is cancelled, so automatically we refunded them the difference. But later on from your end (CS) you initiated a full refund, which was applied to the first higher order amount. And this is what creates the debt as the balance thinks that we have returned the full amount to the user, meaning whatever the user previously paid was all returned to them. But since a service was provided to the user for the order or cancellation fee, it is still trying to charge the user for the extra refunded amount. That is where the debt comes from.

Could you complete a refund to the user’s balance on a different order to compensate for the debt in their account?

Hello Team!

I completely understand why this might look like a double charge, but I can assure you that the user was only charged once. This is a common part of how card payments are processed. Here's what happens:

# When the user first makes a payment, the bank temporarily ‘reserves' the funds and this is just the bank setting aside the amount for the transaction. The user’s account balance might show less amount but the payment hasn’t actually been taken out by the bank yet.
# Later, when the payment is fully processed, that reserved amount is now “officially” debited from the user’s account. At that point, some banks send a second notification, which can make it seem like a second charge.


I would advise the user to check their final account balance or statement, where they can confirm that only one payment was actually withdrawn. The earlier “pending” amount will either drop off or convert into the final charge.

Cheers,
Afiba

Hey,

In Hungary we have commission netting.

_Through commission netting, your campaigns/bonuses/compensations are reflected as a discount from your commission, instead of each having their individual invoices. Simply, your commission is reduced in the amount of your campaigns/bonuses/compensations - ensuring a more clear invoicing process, and less invoicing noise._

_For example, previously you would see a commission of 416.91€ and separate bonus lines of 11€ on your invoice, which totaled up to 361.92€. Now, you would only see a single row of commission in the amount of 361.92€, meaning the calculation is already done in the background._

Nikolay Roll

I’d like to have your view on this ticket? All the information is in the ticket, but to recap:

LMDVTC is moving their fleet to a *cooperative structure* which they believe will help them adapt to the likely upcoming regulations requiring fleets to employ their drivers. They’re asking for Bolt’s involvement — initially to use our name for legitimacy and potentially take a seat in one of their decision-making “collèges,” and later possibly to provide financial incentives encouraging driver exclusivity. 

They seem to be *using the end of the Captive Fleet project as an opportunity to push for our involvement in their cooperative*. The reasoning behind this is that, as the Captive Fleet winds down, LMDVTC faces the challenge of terminating the contracts of currently employed drivers — a process that carries *legal, administrative, and reputational risks*. Large-scale terminations could attract *DREETS scrutiny*, and LMDVTC suggests this could indirectly reflect on Bolt given our close association with the project. By moving these drivers into the cooperative instead, they argue they can *avoid complex redundancies*, *preserve employment continuity and benefits*, and *reframe the transition* as a socially responsible restructuring. They position this as beneficial for both the drivers and Bolt, presenting the cooperative as a way to *minimize exposure while maintaining goodwill*.

They say both *URSSAF* and their *lawyers* have validated the model. 

The urgency is growing, as other fleets are beginning to explore similar setups. There’s a *meeting with LMDVTC on Friday the 21st*, and before that we need a *legal assessment* to understand:

* If Bolt can *participate in a cooperative* legally.
* Whether such a model could *reduce reclassification risks*.
* If it could *help meet future regulations* on driver employment.

Given the sensitiveness of this topic, do you agree if I ask Arthur to provide a fee quote for a short analysis (one-pager) so that we can share this internally with Etienne? 

Happy to further discuss during our 1:1 today.

Couple of logics we need to figure out for campaign business voucher profiling. One is failed payments and other one is business order counts. 

Failed payments query below, order count one will be added soon:



{noformat}--business vouchers/failed payments/UNION excluded

WITH rates AS (
  SELECT
  currency,
  CAST(valid_on AS date) AS day,
  rate
  FROM ng_public_spark.currency_exchange_rates
  WHERE currency <> 'EUR'
  AND CAST(valid_on AS date) >= date_add(current_date, -7))
SELECT
  bbc.id AS business_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN pr.created >= date_add(current_date, -1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_payments_count_1day,
  COUNT(*) AS failed_payments_count_7day,
  MAX(CASE WHEN pr.created >= date_add(current_date, -1) THEN CASE
                  WHEN p.currency = 'EUR' THEN pr.amount
                  ELSE CASE WHEN r.rate IS NULL OR r.rate = 0 THEN NULL ELSE pr.amount / r.rate END
                END
      END) AS max_failed_payment_in_eur_1day,
  MAX(CASE
        WHEN p.currency = 'EUR' THEN pr.amount
        ELSE CASE WHEN r.rate IS NULL OR r.rate = 0 THEN NULL ELSE pr.amount / r.rate END
      END) AS max_failed_payment_in_eur_7days
FROM ng_public_spark.business_business_company bbc
JOIN ng_public_spark.payment_payment_user pu ON pu.external_id = bbc.id AND pu.type = 'business'
JOIN ng_public_spark.payment_payment_order po ON po.payment_user_id = pu.id
JOIN ng_public_spark.payment_payment p ON p.payment_order_id = po.id
JOIN ng_public_spark.payment_payment_row pr ON pr.id = p.last_payment_row_id
AND pr.state = 'error'
AND pr.type  <> 'chargeback'
AND pr.created >= date_add(current_date, -7)
LEFT JOIN rates r ON p.currency <> 'EUR' AND p.currency = r.currency
AND CAST(date_trunc('day', pr.created) AS date) = r.day
WHERE CAST(pr.created_date AS date) >= date_add(current_date, -7)
GROUP BY bbc.id
ORDER BY failed_payments_count_7day DESC;{noformat}

** If Bolt balance refund is successful, there is a green button after the refund “🟢 success”
** If refund to card, 💳 success
* Check if the payment method used to make the order is not a business account. In this case, the refund will be sent to the business account balance.
* Check if the user did not spend their refund on a next order (or orders) for Bolt balance refunds
* Check if the user did not have a previous debt or previous failed payment that was covered up with the refund
* If refund was sent to Balance instead of card, check first if payment was made from card. Usually, if card payment fails, card refund also fails. Sometimes refund will be sent to balance in cases payment was charged from balance first as debt and the refund will clear the debt previously created by the balance charge. 
* Check [payment page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/1946767063], to ensure there are no errors on the refund and advise the user to check with their bank if card refund was successfully completed.

+*BACKGROUND*+

* Bolt is intending to launch W4W in Germany. RFC is [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PLBK/pages/3978625480/Women+for+Women+W4W+category].
** Intention is to do the test launch next week (unfortunately, we were only looped in today :melting_face: )
** Test launch will focus specifically on ‘trusted fleets with female employees’.
* Question from Ops is *whether we can ask the driver if they are male/female/diverse*.
** This would involve adding a gender field into the registration flow - we would +*not*+ be asking fr supporting evidence (e.g., IDs). We would provide a checkbox asking the driver which they best identified with. This would not be specific to W4W - it would be part of the regular signup flow.
*** Gender won’t be displayed on profile. Drivers can request a change via email.
** Apparently this is already “_standardised across countries_”. Question is whether we can make this change to the registration flow in Germany.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* *Asking for gender during registration flow*: This is generally fine ✅ 
** Gender data is not sensitive, and it is coming directly from the driver. Clearly mentioned in the driver privacy notice, legal basis is legitimate interest, and collection of the data is clearly proportionate for the purpose being pursued. We are not using any ADM here, as IDs are not involved. Also, not being overshared, since not visible on the profile. Drivers can also exercise DSRRs here.
*** NB. It does not appear that German laws place any obvious restrictions on collecting gender data in this context.
** Nevertheless, worth digging into what happens if someone selects ‘diverse’.
* *W4W in Germany - General*: This is generally fine ✅ 
** W4W feature has been previously assessed from a privacy POV - determined that no LIA / DPIA needed for now.
** Main issue always concerns *collection of ID docs / personal identity codes* (see e.g., [+LSS-55254+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-55254]). 
*** If this is not happening here, this significantly de-risks the feature, as that is usually the blocker. However, worth checking.
*** NB. There is technically a risk regarding accuracy here - if we don’t check ID, how do we verify their claims? However, this is level-weighing against the risks of collecting ID docs.
** Also these is a risk of *exclusion / discrimination*. Drivers may argue that: (a) they are being excluded from W4W; and/or (b) Bolt is limiting / mischaracterising their gender. In response to these issues:
*** (a) The whole point of W4W is that it is women-based. Excluding people who are not women is the whole point from a safety POV. Drivers are not otherwise being prevented from conducting trips - W4W is but a small subset of Bolt’s service.
*** (b) In Germany, the third gender option “diverse” is the official term recognised by the government (see [+here+|https://www.antidiskriminierungsstelle.de/EN/about-discrimination/grounds-for-discrimination/gender-and-gender-identity/third-option/third-option-node.html]). As such, the options are proportionate.

+*NEXT STEPS*+

* Questions:
** Where did the previous discussions with Legal happen? This might help focus the SD ticket discussion.
** How did we verify the gender of the trusted female employees - presumably this is the fleet telling us this? Were any ID codes / ID docs involved? I’m conscious that in other countries we collect ID from _riders_ for W4W - so what is the ‘standard approach’?
** What happens if someone selects ‘diverse’?
* Re asking for gender in the registration flow, we can do this ✅ 
* Re W4W as a whole, I need to see what Legal has advised already (?) 
** However, provided that we are not collecting IDs / ID codes from drivers, I fail to see how this would be blocked from a _privacy_ POV. There may be some separate safety considerations - otherwise I think this is fine.

Thank you for your comments regarding liability and data protection in the context of our cooperation. We fully understand your concerns about potential liability risks and the need for protection against any employee misconduct. However, we would like to clarify why it is *legally and structurally not possible* for Worksmart to assume contractual liability for the conduct of the assigned employees under the framework of temporary employment.

 

# *Legal Roles under Temporary Employment Law*

According to the *German Temporary Employment Act (AÜG)*, the employee remains legally employed by Worksmart but is *integrated operationally and professionally into your organization (Bolt)*. This means that:

* Bolt exercises the *right to issue work instructions*,
* Bolt is responsible for the *actual supervision and direction of the work*,
* Worksmart is responsible for *salary payment, social contributions, and employment law obligations*.

As a result, Worksmart *cannot be held liable for the actual performance or potential mistakes of the employee*, since these occur *under your direct supervision*. Assigning such liability to Worksmart would contradict the legal structure and case law governing temporary employment relationships.

# *Practical Liability Framework*

In practice, the standard approach is that:

* Worksmart is liable for the *proper selection and provision* of the employee (e.g., in cases of demonstrable negligence in the recruitment process),
* However, *the professional performance and conduct* of the employee are under Bolt’s responsibility, as you direct their daily work.

This division ensures a *legally compliant and economically balanced* allocation of risk between the parties.

# *Data Protection*

The same principle applies to data protection:

* Worksmart remains the employer and ensures that the employee is *bound by confidentiality and data protection obligations*.
* Once the employee is deployed at Bolt, they process personal data *under Bolt’s responsibility* as the *data controller* within the meaning of the GDPR.
* Therefore, Worksmart *cannot assume responsibility for data processing activities* carried out within Bolt’s operational environment, as these are outside of our control.

 

*In summary:*
A broad assumption of liability by Worksmart for the conduct or errors of the assigned employees is *not legally permissible*, as those employees act under your supervision and control during their assignment. However, Worksmart will continue to ensure that it *fulfills its own obligations diligently* and that all employees are properly vetted and bound by confidentiality and data protection requirements.

Accordingly, *termination and blocking are justified*: threats made against Bolt’s facilities or employees constitute both a breach of Clause 2.1.6 (use for unlawful purposes) and grounds for action under *Clause 13.3* (damage to Bolt’s brand and business).

Please ensure proper documentation of this case — our internal records should clearly reflect the threats or misconduct, referencing the specific breaches above. The driver should have also received a termination notice citing these contractual provisions.

Many thanks,

Beatriz L.

Hello, Eva! We are moving into a direction where we will start using issue keys instead of issue titles. The reason for that is that issue keys don’t change in the system, while associated issue titles can change. Issue keys are also the most basic id of an issue title (it is like support case id and support case url in Looker). 



All new dashboards that contain issue keys or titles will actually contain a link to the mapping of issue keys to issue titles, where you can find the relevant issue key for your issue title. 



Additionally, if you need to filter for a specific issue key, please use Case Issue Keys *contains* specific issue key. That will give you all support cases that have that issue key. 



Hope that helps!

Sharing an example of the user tracking sophistication needed for incremental testing for big brands.



h4. The "User X" Journey: Why Our Tracking Needs Are More Complex

Today, we mostly care about what happens in a single session. For performance ads (CPA/CPC), we need to track a user's behaviour across multiple sessions and over time.

Here’s a typical journey for User X, who has different "food missions":

h4. Monday (Discovery Mission):

* User X opens the app, not sure what to eat.
* They see a Hero Banner ad (Awareness, CPM) for "McDonald's New Spicy Burger."
* They don't click. They browse a few stores and close the app.
* Today's Tracking: We might log an impression, but it's not connected to anything.
* 2026 Ad Need: We must log that User X saw this ad and store it against their profile.

h4. Wednesday (Search Mission):

* User X is now craving a burger. They open the app and search for "burger."
* They see a Sponsored Search ad (Performance, CPC) for the "McDonald's New Spicy Burger" at the top.
* They click the ad, browse the menu, but get a phone call and abandon their cart.
* Today's Tracking: We see a click and a lost session.
* 2026 Ad Need: We _must_ log that User X clicked this specific ad, adding it to their profile history.

h4. Friday (Conversion Mission):

* User X remembers the burger. They open the app, _do not search_, navigate directly to the McDonald's store page (an "organic" visit), and buy the Spicy Burger.
* Today's Tracking: This appears to be a 100% organic, free conversion for McDonald's. We get no credit

h4. *The Tracking Gap We Need to Close*

* To get paid, we must prove to McDonald's that the ad they paid for on Wednesday (or even the ad they showed on Monday) was responsible for the order on Friday.
* This requires a completely new capability: Cross-Session Attribution.
* We need to be able to "look back" from the Friday order and connect it to User X's ad interactions from Wednesday and Monday. This is the only way a CPA/CPC model works.
* This new level of tracking requires us to collect, store, and process user data in a manner that our current Terms and Conditions likely do not cover. This is the time-consuming legal and privacy problem we need to solve _before_ we can build the product.

The customer used an APM (Alternative Payment Method) to place the order and this type of payment methods does not have a preauthorisation option that is later reversed. They only support a direct charge on the card. So if the user makes an order but then cancels it, in this case we refund their money unlike preauthorisation where we just release the reserved amount. 
So in this case, the user placed an order and we charged them higher, but at the end of the ride, the order price decreased or the order is cancelled, so automatically we refunded them the difference. But later on from your end (CS) you initiated a full refund, which was applied to the first higher order amount. And this is what creates the debt as the balance thinks that we have returned the full amount to the user, meaning whatever the user previously paid was all returned to them. But since a service was provided to the user for the order or cancellation fee, it is still trying to charge the user for the extra refunded amount. That is where the debt comes from.

Could you complete a refund to the user’s balance on a different order to compensate for the debt in their account?

 {{users_created_local}} field it’s unfortunately not very reliable. The timestamp depends on the user having a {{city_id}} (since that’s used to determine their local timezone), but many users don’t have a city assigned. Because of that, the “local” creation time isn’t accurate for a large portion of users.
What we _can_ rely on is {{users_created_utc}}, which represents the actual account creation time in UTC. However, this field hasn’t been added to any of the marts yet, so it’s not directly available for reporting or analysis at the moment.

The engineering team is currently working on implementing the automated tool and [~accountid:5bc9c1000e133108f3311acd] has requested for a few additional clarifications. I’ve listed all the questions below for your review and feedback.

Questions:


# Would the drivers be liable for taxes on the monthly DPWRA top-up? Should we display the DPWRA top-up as a separate line item on the monthly partner invoice (example [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1who_djuAmGA5ouOyDd4nYtSgqPSR__J6xrnckTbRgkw/edit?usp=sharing])?

# Should the DPWRA top up be explicitly shown on the monthly earning statement on the driver app (example [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1SkL687RDmUzfoe8S2oWoX_0PYrGxS-M7U-mnhoY0irY/edit?usp=sharing])? Should it go under the ‘other income’ header?

# In the UK, any amount refunded to the rider (and deducted from the driver’s earnings) due to driver fault is excluded from DPWRA top-up calculations. Would applying the same approach be acceptable for Canada?
Additionally, should such orders be *completely excluded* from the DPWRA calculation (including the active time spent on them), or should we *only exclude the refunded portion*?
For instance, consider an order where the driver initially earns CAD 10, but a refund of CAD 4 is issued to the rider due to the driver’s fault and deducted from the driver’s earnings. For the purpose of DPWRA top-up calculations, should the driver’s earnings be considered as CAD 10 or CAD 6?
If we include such an order in the DPWRA calculation and treat the earnings as CAD 6, we may be required to compensate the driver through the DPWRA top-up to bring their pay up to the minimum threshold. This could inadvertently incentivize misuse or fraudulent behavior.

# For trips with anomalous or invalid data that will be excluded from DPWRA top-up calculations, below is the template of the automated notification email (sent monthly) that will be sent to affected drivers to inform them of the exclusion. Bolt representative
